key_insight: HiSkill turns past interactions into a hierarchical skill graph so an LLM agent can reuse high-level skills and ground them into executable actions more effectively.
engineering_relevance: The framework is useful for long-horizon agent systems because it improves task execution while reducing inference token usage through structured skill retrieval and guidance.
method: Builds a directed graph with skill nodes, AtomicOp nodes, and typed edges.
Models decomposition, temporal transition, compatibility, support, and recovery relations.
Retrieves a compact task-relevant subgraph and uses it to guide skill switching and action grounding during execution.
evidence_signal: The paper reports experiments on three interactive environments, where HiSkill outperforms state-of-the-art baselines and uses fewer inference tokens.
watch_item: Graph construction and subgraph retrieval may add implementation complexity and require careful design to avoid noisy or incomplete skill relations.
paper_title: HiSkill: Empowering LLM Agents with Hierarchical Skill Graphs
